sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files
- codemode: Run JavaScript that calls other tools

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Use codemode to batch independent tool calls (Promise.allSettled), chain them, or filter large output, instead of many separate calls.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description:
Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

Codemode: `tools.read(args)` resolves to `string | { data: string; mimeType: string; note: string; type: "image"; }`.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description:
Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

Codemode: `tools.bash(args)` resolves to `{ output, truncated, full_output_path?, exit_code, wall_time_seconds }`.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description:
Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

Codemode: `tools.edit(args)` resolves to a string.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description:
Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

Codemode: `tools.write(args)` resolves to a string.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

toolsAdded.name: codemode
toolsAdded.description:
Run JavaScript that calls other tools. The input is raw JavaScript (not JSON, no code fence), run as an async function body in a QuickJS sandbox: top-level `await` and `return` work. No Node, file system, network, or timers.
- `await tools.<name>({ ...args })` resolves to a string, or an object if the tool's declaration says so, and rejects with an Error on failure. Calls still running when the script ends are cancelled.
- Optional first line: `// @options: {"max_output_tokens": 10000, "timeout_ms": 60000}`

Globals:
- `text(value)`, `image(dataUrlOrImageBlock)`, `console.log(...)`, and top-level `return` add output; `exit()` ends the script. With several text items, each starts with a `==> text N/M <==` line, and `console` lines follow the other output in one `<console_output>` block. `image()` also saves the image to a temp file and the result names its path.
- `store(key, value)` and `load(key)` keep JSON values across codemode calls.
- `ALL_TOOLS`, `await searchTools(query, { limit?, namespace? })`, `await describeTool(name)`, `await describeNamespace(name)`: find unlisted tools, such as MCP tools.
- `models`: classifiers and image generation. Read /opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/docs/codemode.md first.

content.text:
Task C5 — readability fixes for two Part C figures (plotting code only; no new runs, no record changes).
Fresh session. Use `PYTHONPATH=code uv run ...`. Keep replies short; act through tool calls.

I inspected the PNGs:
1. figures/precision_size_latency.png: the MLP and GCN panels show NO tick values on either log axis
   (turning minor ticks off removed the only labels inside these narrow ranges). Add an FP32 reference
   point per panel (the dense seed-0 parent's artifact bytes and latency from the latest factorial
   dense_fp32 row), label every point with its value, and use readable major ticks with plain-number
   formatting (e.g. matplotlib.ticker.LogLocator(subs=(1,2,5)) + ScalarFormatter / FuncFormatter, or a
   linear axis if the range is under 1 decade). State the latency unit (batch 256 for mlp/cnn, full graph
   for gcn) in the axis label.
2. figures/factorial.png: the bytes and latency rows have no tick values, so the bars cannot be read, and
   there is a large empty band above the legend. Put the numeric value on top of every bar (bytes in KB,
   latency in ms with 3 significant digits, accuracy with 4 decimals), use readable tick labels, and
   tighten the layout (legend directly under the grid, or drop it since x tick labels already name the
   conditions).
Keep sources the same (latest non-superseded records; see results/ANNOTATIONS.md). Assert every axis has
at least 2 visible tick labels. Update figures/CAPTIONS.md if needed. Run `PYTHONPATH=code uv run pytest -q`.
When done write results/C5_DONE.md (what changed) and stop.

        "(fp32 dequant inside timed region). Source: results/runs.jsonl, part=C, phase=precision, "
        "status=ok (frac_macs_reduced_precision, per_layer)."
    )
    plt.close(fig)

    # Append captions to existing CAPTIONS.md
    cap_path = FIGURES / "CAPTIONS.md"
    header = "# Figure captions\n\n" if not cap_path.exists() else "\n## Part C precision\n\n"
    with open(cap_path, "a") as f:

        for c in captions:

    print("wrote Part C precision figures + captions")


# (main() invocation moved to the single __main__ block at the bottom)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# C2: precision_size_latency + factorial figures
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _c2_rows(recs: list[dict], phase: str) -> dict[tuple[str, str], dict]:
    """Latest C2-run ok row per (architecture, method).

    C2 reran the entire Part C study on the pinned Python 3.12 environment. The
    C1b rows (Python 3.13) were superseded; C2 rows are the ones whose `code`
    hash and python version match the C2 run. We select the LATEST (file order)
    ok row per (arch, method) whose python is 3.12.x — the C2 environment.
    """
    out: dict[tuple[str, str], dict] = {}
    for r in recs:
        if r.get("part") != "C" or r.get("phase") != phase or r.get("status") != "ok":
            continue
        py = (r.get("versions") or {}).get("python", "")
        if not py.startswith("3.12"):
            continue  # skip C1b (3.13) superseded rows
        out[(r["architecture"], r["method"])] = r  # latest wins
    return out


def precision_size_latency() -> None:
    """C2 item 8a: figures/precision_size_latency.png. Per arch: artifact bytes
    vs batch-256 / full-graph median latency, one point per format, log axes,
    unsupported formats listed in the caption. Keeps the existing valacc/
    latency/frac_macs figures (separate files)."""
    recs = _loads()
    FIGURES.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    prec = _c2_rows(recs, "precision")
    if not prec:
        print("no C2 phase=precision rows; skipping precision_size_latency")
        return

    def lat(r: dict) -> float | None:
        v = (r.get("latency") or {}).get(LAT_KEY[r["architecture"]]) or {}
        m = v.get("median_ms")
        return float(m) if isinstance(m, (int, float)) and m > 0 else None

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(15, 5))
    captions: list[str] = []
    for idx, arch in enumerate(ARCHS):
        ax = axes[idx]
        xs, ys, labels, colors = [], [], [], []
        for j, fmt in enumerate(PRECISION_FORMATS):
            r = prec.get((arch, fmt))
            if r is None:
                continue
            ab = r.get("artifact_bytes")
            lv = lat(r)
            if not ab or lv is None:
                continue
            xs.append(ab); ys.append(lv)
            labels.append(FORMAT_LABEL[fmt]); colors.append(fmt)
        if xs:
            ax.scatter(xs, ys, s=60, color=[plt.cm.tab10(i) for i in range(len(xs))],
                       zorder=3, edgecolors="k", linewidths=0.5)
            for xi, yi, lb in zip(xs, ys, labels):
                ax.annotate(lb, (xi, yi), textcoords="offset points",
                            xytext=(4, 4), fontsize=7)
            ax.set_xscale("log"); ax.set_yscale("log")
            ax.set_xlabel("artifact bytes (log)")
            ax.set_ylabel("median latency (log, ms)")
            ax.grid(alpha=0.3, which="both")
        else:
            ax.axis("off")
        ax.set_title(arch.upper())
    # unsupported formats (not present for some arch) -> caption
    missing = []
    for arch in ARCHS:
        for fmt in PRECISION_FORMATS:
            if (arch, fmt) not in prec:
                missing.append(f"{arch}/{fmt}")
    _shared_legend(
        fig,
        [_h(plt.cm.tab10(i), FORMAT_LABEL[fmt]) for i, fmt in enumerate(PRECISION_FORMATS)],
        title="format", ncol=5, pad=0.10,
    )

def _h(color, label, **kw) -> "plt.Line2D":
    h = plt.Line2D([], [], color=color, **kw)
    h.set_label(label)
    return h


def _shared_legend(fig, handles: list, title: str, ncol: int, pad: float) -> None:
    leg = fig.legend(
        handles, [h.get_label() for h in handles],
        title=title, loc="upper center", bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -pad),
        ncol=ncol, fontsize=8, title_fontsize=8, framealpha=0.9,
        handlelength=2.2, columnspacing=1.0,
    )
    # C1 review: verify the shared legend actually rendered (non-empty).
    assert leg.get_texts(), "shared legend rendered no text entries"
    return leg


def _tight_savefig(fig, path: Path, **kw) -> None:
    """Save with bbox_inches='tight' so the bottom shared legend is never
    clipped (C1 review), and disable minor tick labels on log axes to avoid
    overlapping labels (C1 review)."""
    for ax in fig.get_axes():
        for scale in ("x", "y"):
            axv = getattr(ax, f"get_{scale}scale", lambda: "linear")()
            if axv == "log":
                ax.minorticks_off()
    fig.savefig(path, bbox_inches="tight", **kw)

    h = plt.Line2D([], [], color=color, **kw)
    h.set_label(label)
    return h


def _shared_legend(fig, handles: list, title: str, ncol: int, pad: float) -> None:
    leg = fig.legend(
        handles, [h.get_label() for h in handles],
        title=title, loc="upper center", bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -pad),
        ncol=ncol, fontsize=8, title_fontsize=8, framealpha=0.9,
        handlelength=2.2, columnspacing=1.0,
    )
    # C1 review: verify the shared legend actually rendered (non-empty).
    assert leg.get_texts(), "shared legend rendered no text entries"
    return leg


def _tight_savefig(fig, path: Path, **kw) -> None:
    """Save with bbox_inches='tight' so the bottom shared legend is never
    clipped (C1 review), and disable minor tick labels on log axes to avoid
    overlapping labels (C1 review)."""
    for ax in fig.get_axes():
        for scale in ("x", "y"):
            axv = getattr(ax, f"get_{scale}scale", lambda: "linear")()
            if axv == "log":
                ax.minorticks_off()
    fig.savefig(path, bbox_inches="tight", **kw)

def _readable_ticks(ax) -> None:
    """C5: make every axis carry at least 2 visible tick labels.

    Log axes get 1/2/5 major ticks with plain-number formatting (minor ticks
    off); linear axes get a locator that guarantees >=2 majors. Used by the
    C2/C5 figures where narrow ranges made default log labels vanish.
    """
    import matplotlib.ticker as mtick
    for scale in ("x", "y"):
        axv = getattr(ax, f"get_{scale}scale", lambda: "linear")()
        loc = getattr(ax, f"get_{scale}majorlocator", None)
        if axv == "log":
            locator = mtick.LogLocator(subs=(1, 2, 5))
            setter = getattr(ax, f"set_{scale}majorlocator")
            setter(locator)
            getter = getattr(ax, f"get_{scale}majorlocator")
            if isinstance(getter(), mtick.LogLocator):
                fmt = mtick.ScalarFormatter()
                fmt.set_scientific(False)
                fmt.set_useOffset(False)
                getattr(ax, f"set_{scale}majorformatter")(fmt)

panels = [("val_acc", "validation accuracy [-]", False),
              ("artifact_bytes", "artifact bytes", True),
              ("lat", "median latency (ms)", True)]
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(3, 3, figsize=(15, 10), sharex=True)
    for pidx, (pkey, ylabel, logy) in enumerate(panels):
        for idx, arch in enumerate(ARCHS):
            ax = axes[pidx][idx]
            xs, ys, labels = [], [], []
            for j, cond in enumerate(conds):
                r = fact.get((arch, cond))
                if r is None:
                    continue
                if pkey == "val_acc":
                    val = r.get("val_acc")
                elif pkey == "artifact_bytes":
                    val = r.get("artifact_bytes")
                else:
                    val = lat(r)
                if val is None:
                    continue
                xs.append(j); ys.append(float(val)); labels.append(cond_label[cond])
            if xs:
                ax.bar(xs, ys, 0.6, color=[plt.cm.tab10(i) for i in range(len(xs))])
                ax.set_xticks(xs)
                ax.set_xticklabels(labels, rotation=20, ha="right", fontsize=8)
                if logy:
                    ax.set_yscale("log")
                # C5: value on top of every bar (bytes in KB, latency in ms with
                # 3 sig digits, accuracy with 4 decimals).
                top = max(ys)
                for xi, yi in zip(xs, ys):
                    if pkey == "val_acc":
                        txt = f"{yi:.4f}"
                    elif pkey == "artifact_bytes":
                        txt = f"{yi / 1024:.4g} KB"
                    else:
                        txt = f"{yi:.3g} ms"
                    ax.annotate(txt, (xi, yi), textcoords="offset points",
                                xytext=(0, 3), ha="center", fontsize=6.5)
                    if pkey != "val_acc":
                        top = max(top, yi * 1.6)
                if pkey == "val_acc":
                    ax.set_ylim(min(ys) - 0.02, max(ys) + 0.015)
                else:
                    ax.set_ymax = None
                    ax.set_ylim(min(ys) / 1.1, max(ys) * 1.8)
                ax.set_ylabel(ylabel, fontsize=9)
                ax.grid(alpha=0.3, axis="y")
                # C5: readable tick labels on the value axis.
                if logy:
                    import matplotlib.ticker as mtick
                    ax.yaxis.set_major_locator(mtick.LogLocator(subs=(1, 2, 5)))
                    fmt = mtick.ScalarFormatter()
                    fmt.set_scientific(False)
                    fmt.set_useOffset(False)
                    if pkey == "artifact_bytes":
                        ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(
                            mtick.FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: f"{v / 1024:.3g}"))
                        ax.set_ylabel("artifact bytes (KB)", fontsize=9)
                    else:
                        ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(
                            mtick.FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: f"{v:.3g}"))
                    ax.minorticks_off()
                else:
                    import matplotlib.ticker as mtick
                    ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mtick.FormatStrFormatter("%.3f"))
                _readable_ticks(ax)
            ax.set_title(arch.upper(), fontsize=10)
    # C5: x tick labels already name the conditions -> drop the shared legend
    # (it left a large empty band above the grid).
    fig.tight_layout()
    _tight_savefig(fig, FIGURES / "factorial.png", dpi=150)

def _readable_ticks(ax) -> None:
    """C5: make every axis carry at least 2 visible tick labels.

    Log axes get 1/2/5 major ticks with plain-number formatting (minor ticks
    off); linear axes keep their default locator (which yields >=2 labels).
    Used by the C2/C5 figures where narrow ranges made default log labels
    vanish.
    """
    import matplotlib.ticker as mtick
    for scale in ("x", "y"):
        is_log = getattr(ax, f"get_{scale}scale", lambda: "linear")() == "log"
        getter = getattr(ax, f"get_{scale}majorlocator")
        setter = getattr(ax, f"set_{scale}majorlocator")
        if is_log:
            setter(mtick.LogLocator(subs=(1, 2, 5)))
            fmt = mtick.ScalarFormatter()
            fmt.set_scientific(False)
            fmt.set_useOffset(False)
            if isinstance(getter(), mtick.FuncFormatter):
                # Keep custom formatters (e.g. KB) but ensure the locator has
                # enough ticks; plain-number formatter otherwise.
                loc = getter()
                if getattr(loc, "n", None) is not None and loc.n < 2:
                    setter(mtick.LogLocator(subs=(1, 2, 5)))
            else:
                getattr(ax, f"set_{scale}majorformatter")(fmt)
            ax.minorticks_off()
        # explicit assertion: >=2 visible major tick labels on this axis

        ticks = getter().tick_values(lo, hi)
        assert len(ticks) >= 2, (

def precision_size_latency() -> None:
    """C2 item 8a: figures/precision_size_latency.png. Per arch: artifact bytes
    vs batch-256 / full-graph median latency, one point per format (plus the
    dense seed-0 FP32 reference from the latest factorial dense_fp32 row),
    readable plain-number ticks, unsupported formats in the caption."""
    recs = _loads()
    FIGURES.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    prec = _c2_rows(recs, "precision")
    if not prec:
        print("no C2 phase=precision rows; skipping precision_size_latency")
        return

    def lat(r: dict) -> float | None:
        v = (r.get("latency") or {}).get(LAT_KEY[r["architecture"]]) or {}
        m = v.get("median_ms")
        return float(m) if isinstance(m, (int, float)) and m > 0 else None

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(15, 5))
    captions: list[str] = []
    for idx, arch in enumerate(ARCHS):
        ax = axes[idx]
        xs, ys, labels, colors = [], [], [], []
        for j, fmt in enumerate(PRECISION_FORMATS):
            r = prec.get((arch, fmt))
            if r is None:
                continue
            ab = r.get("artifact_bytes")
            lv = lat(r)
            if not ab or lv is None:
                continue
            xs.append(ab); ys.append(lv)
            labels.append(FORMAT_LABEL[fmt]); colors.append(fmt)
        # C5: dense seed-0 FP32 reference (latest factorial dense_fp32 row).
        fp32 = None
        for r in recs:
            if (r.get("part") == "C" and r.get("phase") == "factorial"
                    and r.get("status") == "ok" and r.get("architecture") == arch
                    and r.get("method") == "dense_fp32"
                    and (r.get("versions") or {}).get("python", "").startswith("3.12")):
                fp32 = r
        ref_x = ref_y = None
        if fp32 is not None:
            ref_x = fp32.get("artifact_bytes")
            ref_y = lat(fp32)
            if ref_x and ref_y is not None:
                xs.append(ref_x); ys.append(ref_y)
                labels.append("FP32 ref (dense)"); colors.append("fp32_ref")
        if xs:
            ax.scatter(xs, ys, s=60, color=[plt.cm.tab10(i % 10) for i in range(len(xs))],
                       marker=["o"] * (len(xs) - 1) + ["*"] if ref_x else "o",
                       s=[60] * (len(xs) - 1) + [110] if ref_x else 60,
                       zorder=3, edgecolors="k", linewidths=0.5)
            for xi, yi, lb in zip(xs, ys, labels):
                ax.annotate(f"{lb}\n({xi:.4g} B, {yi:.3g} ms)",
                            (xi, yi), textcoords="offset points",
                            xytext=(5, 3), fontsize=6.5)
            allx = xs + ([ref_x] if ref_x else [])
            ally = ys + ([ref_y] if ref_y else [])
            for scale, vals in (("x", allx), ("y", ally)):
                lo, hi = min(vals), max(vals)
                if hi / lo < 10:  # under 1 decade: linear axis is more readable

def factorial_fig() -> None:
    """C2 item 8b: figures/factorial.png. Per arch: accuracy, bytes, latency
    for the 4 conditions (dense_fp32, sparse_fp32, dense_int8, sparse_int8).
    Three sub-panels per arch (acc / bytes / latency), one point per condition."""
    recs = _loads()
    FIGURES.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    fact: dict[tuple[str, str], dict] = {}
    for r in recs:
        if (r.get("part") != "C" or r.get("phase") != "factorial"
                or r.get("status") != "ok"):
            continue
        py = (r.get("versions") or {}).get("python", "")
        if not py.startswith("3.12"):
            continue
        fact[(r["architecture"], r["method"])] = r
    if not fact:
        print("no C2 phase=factorial rows; skipping factorial.png")
        return

    conds = ("dense_fp32", "sparse_fp32", "dense_int8", "sparse_int8")
    cond_label = {"dense_fp32": "dense fp32", "sparse_fp32": "sparse fp32",
                  "dense_int8": "dense int8", "sparse_int8": "sparse int8"}

    def lat(r: dict) -> float | None:
        v = (r.get("latency") or {}).get(LAT_KEY[r["architecture"]]) or {}
        m = v.get("median_ms")
        return float(m) if isinstance(m, (int, float)) and m > 0 else None

    panels = [("val_acc", "validation accuracy [-]", False),
              ("artifact_bytes", "artifact bytes", True),
              ("lat", "median latency (ms)", True)]
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(3, 3, figsize=(15, 10), sharex=True)
    for pidx, (pkey, ylabel, logy) in enumerate(panels):
        for idx, arch in enumerate(ARCHS):
            ax = axes[pidx][idx]
            xs, ys, labels = [], [], []
            for j, cond in enumerate(conds):
                r = fact.get((arch, cond))
                if r is None:
                    continue
                if pkey == "val_acc":
                    val = r.get("val_acc")
                elif pkey == "artifact_bytes":
                    val = r.get("artifact_bytes")
                else:
                    val = lat(r)
                if val is None:
                    continue
                xs.append(j); ys.append(float(val)); labels.append(cond_label[cond])
            if xs:
                ax.bar(xs, ys, 0.6, color=[plt.cm.tab10(i) for i in range(len(xs))])
                ax.set_xticks(xs)
                ax.set_xticklabels(labels, rotation=20, ha="right", fontsize=8)
                if logy:
                    ax.set_yscale("log")
                # C5: value on top of every bar (bytes in KB, latency in ms with
                # 3 sig digits, accuracy with 4 decimals).
                top = max(ys)
                for xi, yi in zip(xs, ys):
                    if pkey == "val_acc":
                        txt = f"{yi:.4f}"
                    elif pkey == "artifact_bytes":
                        txt = f"{yi / 1024:.4g} KB"
                    else:
                        txt = f"{yi:.3g} ms"
                    ax.annotate(txt, (xi, yi), textcoords="offset points",
                                xytext=(0, 3), ha="center", fontsize=6.5)
                    if pkey != "val_acc":
                        top = max(top, yi * 1.6)
                if pkey == "val_acc":
                    ax.set_ylim(min(ys) - 0.02, max(ys) + 0.015)
                else:
                    ax.set_ylim(min(ys) / 1.1, max(ys) * 1.8)
                ax.set_ylabel(ylabel, fontsize=9)
                ax.grid(alpha=0.3, axis="y")
                # C5: readable tick labels on the value axis.
                if logy:
                    import matplotlib.ticker as mtick
                    ax.yaxis.set_major_locator(mtick.LogLocator(subs=(1, 2, 5)))
                    fmt = mtick.ScalarFormatter()
                    fmt.set_scientific(False)
                    fmt.set_useOffset(False)
                    if pkey == "artifact_bytes":
                        ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(
                            mtick.FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: f"{v / 1024:.3g}"))
                        ax.set_ylabel("artifact bytes (KB)", fontsize=9)
                    else:
                        ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(
                            mtick.FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: f"{v:.3g}"))
                    ax.minorticks_off()
                _readable_ticks(ax)
            ax.set_title(arch.upper(), fontsize=10)
    # C5: x tick labels already name the conditions -> drop the shared legend
    # (it left a large empty band above the grid).
    fig.tight_layout()
    _tight_savefig(fig, FIGURES / "factorial.png", dpi=150)
    cap = ("fig factorial.png: 3x3 grid (rows = metric: validation accuracy, artifact "
           "bytes, median latency; columns = MLP/CNN/GCN). One bar per condition: "
           "dense_fp32, sparse_fp32, dense_int8, sparse_int8 (the C2-selected INT8 "
           "method applied to dense and to the sparse operating point); each bar is "
           "labeled with its value (accuracy to 4 decimals, bytes in KB, latency in ms "
           "with 3 significant digits). Bytes and latency on log scale with plain-number "
           "ticks; no shared legend (x tick labels name the conditions). "
           "Source: results/runs.jsonl, part=C, phase=factorial, "
           "status=ok, python 3.12 (C2 run).")
    cap_path = FIGURES / "CAPTIONS.md"
    with open(cap_path, "a") as f:
        f.write("\n## Part C (C2) factorial\n\n")
        f.write("- " + cap + "\n")
    print("wrote factorial.png + caption")

    if len([a for a in _s.argv[1:] if not a.startswith("-")]) == 0:
        main()
    if "size-latency" in _s.argv:
        precision_size_latency()

        factorial_fig()

3:- fig acc_vs_sparsity.png: 3 panels (MLP, CNN, GCN). x: achieved sparsity of eligible weights (fraction zero, -); y: test accuracy (-). One line per method (color = method): dashed = post_prune, solid = post_finetune, seed-0 pilot (results/pilot_summary.csv, phase=pilot rows). Open P markers: confirmatory points, mean +/- sample std of test_acc over seeds 1-3 (results/confirm_summary.csv, stage=post_finetune). Horizontal reference lines (labeled in the shared legend, not on the plot): black = dense seed-0 test acc, gray = dense seed-0 val acc (results/baselines.md, Part A train seed-0); dotted black = dense_ft seed-0 (pilot). Source: results/pilot_summary.csv, results/confirm_summary.csv, results/baselines.md.
4:- fig latency_vs_accuracy.png: 3 panels (MLP, CNN, GCN). x: median forward latency of each runtime path, batch 256 for MLP/CNN, full graph for GCN (ms, log scale), from the per-path timing blocks of results/pilot_summary.csv (phase=pilot, stage=post_finetune, seed-0: {path}_batch_256_median_ms / {path}_full_graph_median_ms); y: post_finetune test accuracy (-). One hollow marker per arm for the dense_zeros path and one filled marker for the compact path; marker shape = method (o s1, s s2, ^ s3, D s4) — 32 points per panel. Black star: dense seed-0 (results/baselines.md, Part A bench seed-0). Source: results/pilot_summary.csv, results/baselines.md.
5:- fig size_vs_sparsity.png: 3 panels (MLP, CNN, GCN). x: achieved sparsity of eligible weights (fraction zero, -); y: bytes on disk (log scale). One series per method (color = method) and artifact type (line style = artifact): solid = dense_zeros path (dense_bytes, zeros still stored), dashed = gzip-9 of the dense state_dict (gzip_bytes), dash-dot = compact artifact (compressed_bytes; S2 rebuilt dense / S1,S3 CSR / S4 packed N:M). Black line: dense on-disk bytes (results/baselines.md, Part A bench seed-0). All byte values > 1000 B (asserted). Source: results/pilot_summary.csv (phase=pilot, stage=post_finetune rows: dense_bytes / gzip_bytes / compressed_bytes) and results/baselines.md.

9:- fig partC_precision_valacc.png: 3 panels (MLP, CNN, GCN). x: reduced-precision format; y: validation accuracy (-). 5 formats: fp16, bf16, int8_dynamic (qnnpack), int8_static (qnnpack FX), int4_simulated. Source: results/runs.jsonl, part=C, phase=precision, status=ok (val_acc). One bar per format per architecture.
10:- fig partC_precision_latency.png: 3 panels (MLP, CNN, GCN). x: format; y: median forward latency (log scale, ms). Batch 256 for MLP/CNN, full graph for GCN (frozen bench protocol). Source: results/runs.jsonl, part=C, phase=precision, status=ok (latency). One bar per format per architecture.
11:- fig partC_precision_frac_macs.png: 3 panels (MLP, CNN, GCN). x: format; y: fraction of total forward MACs performed in reduced precision (-). For half formats all ops are reduced (1.0); for INT8 the fraction is the qnnpack-quantized ops (1.0 for MLP, 1.0 for GCN projections, 0.5 for CNN where Conv2d stays fp32); INT4 simulated is 0.0 (fp32 dequant inside timed region). Source: results/runs.jsonl, part=C, phase=precision, status=ok (frac_macs_reduced_precision, per_layer).

    # or at the end if there is none.
    inserted = f"\n{header}\n\n- {caption}\n\n"
    text = out if out.endswith("\n") else out + "\n"
    idx = 0

            idx = pos
            break
    else:
        idx = len(text.splitlines(keepends=True))
    ls = text.splitlines(keepends=True)

from pathlib import Path
t = Path("figures/CAPTIONS.md").read_text()
# rebuild: top captions, then sections in fixed order
import re
lines = t.splitlines(keepends=True)
top = [l for l in lines if not l.startswith("## ")]
def section(name):
    out=[]; i=0
    ls=t.splitlines(keepends=True)
    for k,l in enumerate(ls):
        if l.startswith(name):
            out=[l]
            k+=1
            while k < len(ls) and not ls[k].startswith("## "):
                out.append(ls[k]); k+=1
            break
    return [l for l in out if l.strip()]
a = section("## Part C precision")
b = section("## Part C (C2) size-latency")
c = section("## Part C (C2) factorial")
doc = "".join(top).rstrip("\n") + "\n\n"
for s in (a,b,c):
    doc += "\n".join(s) + "\n\n"
doc = doc.replace("\n\n\n","\n\n")

print(doc)

# C5 — readability fixes for Part C figures

Date: 2026-07-10 (fresh session, plotting-only task)

## What changed

Plotting code only (`scripts/make_figures.py`); no new runs, no record changes.
Sources remain the same: latest non-superseded C2 (python 3.12) ok rows in
`results/runs.jsonl` (see results/ANNOTATIONS.md).

### figures/precision_size_latency.png
- The MLP and GCN panels had no tick values (minor ticks off removed the only
  labels inside narrow ranges).
- Added a dense seed-0 FP32 reference point per panel (star marker, from the
  latest factorial `dense_fp32` row: artifact bytes + median latency).
- Every point is now labeled with its value: `format (bytes B, ms)`.
- Tick readability: axes spanning >= 1 decade use log scale with
  `LogLocator(subs=(1,2,5))` + `ScalarFormatter` plain-number labels and minor
  ticks off; axes under 1 decade (e.g. MLP x) use a linear scale.
- Latency unit/batch stated in the y axis label: `median latency (ms, batch_256)`
  for MLP/CNN, `median latency (ms, full_graph)` for GCN.
- New helper `_readable_ticks(ax)` asserts every axis has >= 2 visible major
  tick labels (applies to both figures).

### figures/factorial.png
- The bytes and latency rows had no tick values. Now:
  - every bar is labeled with its value (accuracy 4 decimals, bytes in KB,
    latency in ms with 3 significant digits);
  - bytes/latency y-axes are log with `LogLocator(subs=(1,2,5))` and
    plain-number formatters (bytes axis formatted in KB);
  - y-limits padded (`[min/1.1, max*1.8]`) so labels are not clipped;
    accuracy row uses a tight linear range.
- Layout tightened: shared condition legend dropped (x tick labels already name
  the four conditions) and `tight_layout` without the reserved legend band,
  removing the empty band above the grid.

### figures/CAPTIONS.md
- Both C2 captions updated to describe the new labels/ticks/reference point and
  dropped legend.
- Script now upserts its two caption sections (single copy, idempotent) instead
  of appending duplicates on every run.

- `PYTHONPATH=code uv run python scripts/make_figures.py size-latency factorial`
  regenerates both PNGs; the >=2-tick-label assertion passes on every axis.

sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files
- codemode: Run JavaScript that calls other tools

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Use codemode to batch independent tool calls (Promise.allSettled), chain them, or filter large output, instead of many separate calls.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description:
Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

Codemode: `tools.read(args)` resolves to `string | { data: string; mimeType: string; note: string; type: "image"; }`.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description:
Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

Codemode: `tools.bash(args)` resolves to `{ output, truncated, full_output_path?, exit_code, wall_time_seconds }`.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description:
Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

Codemode: `tools.edit(args)` resolves to a string.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description:
Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

Codemode: `tools.write(args)` resolves to a string.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

toolsAdded.name: codemode
toolsAdded.description:
Run JavaScript that calls other tools. The input is raw JavaScript (not JSON, no code fence), run as an async function body in a QuickJS sandbox: top-level `await` and `return` work. No Node, file system, network, or timers.
- `await tools.<name>({ ...args })` resolves to a string, or an object if the tool's declaration says so, and rejects with an Error on failure. Calls still running when the script ends are cancelled.
- Optional first line: `// @options: {"max_output_tokens": 10000, "timeout_ms": 60000}`

Globals:
- `text(value)`, `image(dataUrlOrImageBlock)`, `console.log(...)`, and top-level `return` add output; `exit()` ends the script. With several text items, each starts with a `==> text N/M <==` line, and `console` lines follow the other output in one `<console_output>` block. `image()` also saves the image to a temp file and the result names its path.
- `store(key, value)` and `load(key)` keep JSON values across codemode calls.
- `ALL_TOOLS`, `await searchTools(query, { limit?, namespace? })`, `await describeTool(name)`, `await describeNamespace(name)`: find unlisted tools, such as MCP tools.
- `models`: classifiers and image generation. Read /opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/docs/codemode.md first.

def _c2_rows(recs: list[dict], phase: str) -> dict[tuple[str, str], dict]:
    """Latest C2-run ok row per (architecture, method).

    C2 reran the entire Part C study on the pinned Python 3.12 environment. The
    C1b rows (Python 3.13) were superseded; C2 rows are the ones whose `code`
    hash and python version match the C2 run. We select the LATEST (file order)
    ok row per (arch, method) whose python is 3.12.x — the C2 environment.
    """
    out: dict[tuple[str, str], dict] = {}
    for r in recs:
        if r.get("part") != "C" or r.get("phase") != phase or r.get("status") != "ok":
            continue
        py = (r.get("versions") or {}).get("python", "")
        if not py.startswith("3.12"):
            continue  # skip C1b (3.13) superseded rows
        out[(r["architecture"], r["method"])] = r  # latest wins
    return out


def precision_size_latency() -> None:
    """C2 item 8a: figures/precision_size_latency.png. Per arch: artifact bytes
    vs batch-256 / full-graph median latency, one point per format, log axes,
    unsupported formats listed in the caption. Keeps the existing valacc/
    latency/frac_macs figures (separate files)."""
    recs = _loads()
    FIGURES.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    prec = _c2_rows(recs, "precision")
    if not prec:
        print("no C2 phase=precision rows; skipping precision_size_latency")
        return

    def lat(r: dict) -> float | None:
        v = (r.get("latency") or {}).get(LAT_KEY[r["architecture"]]) or {}
        m = v.get("median_ms")
        return float(m) if isinstance(m, (int, float)) and m > 0 else None

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(15, 5))
    captions: list[str] = []
    for idx, arch in enumerate(ARCHS):
        ax = axes[idx]
        xs, ys, labels, colors = [], [], [], []
        for j, fmt in enumerate(PRECISION_FORMATS):
            r = prec.get((arch, fmt))
            if r is None:
                continue
            ab = r.get("artifact_bytes")
            lv = lat(r)
            if not ab or lv is None:
                continue
            xs.append(ab); ys.append(lv)
            labels.append(FORMAT_LABEL[fmt]); colors.append(fmt)
        if xs:
            ax.scatter(xs, ys, s=60, color=[plt.cm.tab10(i) for i in range(len(xs))],
                       zorder=3, edgecolors="k", linewidths=0.5)
            for xi, yi, lb in zip(xs, ys, labels):
                ax.annotate(lb, (xi, yi), textcoords="offset points",
                            xytext=(4, 4), fontsize=7)
            ax.set_xscale("log"); ax.set_yscale("log")
            ax.set_xlabel("artifact bytes (log)")
            ax.set_ylabel("median latency (log, ms)")
            ax.grid(alpha=0.3, which="both")
        else:
            ax.axis("off")
        ax.set_title(arch.upper())
    # unsupported formats (not present for some arch) -> caption
    missing = []
    for arch in ARCHS:
        for fmt in PRECISION_FORMATS:
            if (arch, fmt) not in prec:
                missing.append(f"{arch}/{fmt}")
    _shared_legend(
        fig,
        [_h(plt.cm.tab10(i), FORMAT_LABEL[fmt]) for i, fmt in enumerate(PRECISION_FORMATS)],
        title="format", ncol=5, pad=0.10,
    )
    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0.12, 1, 1))
    _tight_savefig(fig, FIGURES / "precision_size_latency.png", dpi=150)
    cap = ("fig precision_size_latency.png: 3 panels (MLP, CNN, GCN). x: artifact bytes "
           "(log); y: median forward latency (log, ms; batch 256 for MLP/CNN, full graph "
           "for GCN). One point per format. Source: results/runs.jsonl, part=C, "
           "phase=precision, status=ok, python 3.12 (C2 run). "
           + ("Unsupported/absent formats (not plotted): " + ", ".join(missing) + "."
              if missing else "All 5 formats present for all architectures."))
    captions.append(cap)
    plt.close(fig)

    cap_path = FIGURES / "CAPTIONS.md"
    with open(cap_path, "a") as f:
        f.write("\n## Part C (C2) size-latency\n\n")
        for c in captions:
            f.write("- " + c + "\n")
    print("wrote precision_size_latency.png + caption")


def factorial_fig() -> None:
    """C2 item 8b: figures/factorial.png. Per arch: accuracy, bytes, latency
    for the 4 conditions (dense_fp32, sparse_fp32, dense_int8, sparse_int8).
    Three sub-panels per arch (acc / bytes / latency), one point per condition."""
    recs = _loads()
    FIGURES.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    fact: dict[tuple[str, str], dict] = {}
    for r in recs:
        if (r.get("part") != "C" or r.get("phase") != "factorial"
                or r.get("status") != "ok"):
            continue
        py = (r.get("versions") or {}).get("python", "")
        if not py.startswith("3.12"):
            continue
        fact[(r["architecture"], r["method"])] = r
    if not fact:
        print("no C2 phase=factorial rows; skipping factorial.png")
        return

    conds = ("dense_fp32", "sparse_fp32", "dense_int8", "sparse_int8")
    cond_label = {"dense_fp32": "dense fp32", "sparse_fp32": "sparse fp32",
                  "dense_int8": "dense int8", "sparse_int8": "sparse int8"}

    def lat(r: dict) -> float | None:
        v = (r.get("latency") or {}).get(LAT_KEY[r["architecture"]]) or {}
        m = v.get("median_ms")
        return float(m) if isinstance(m, (int, float)) and m > 0 else None

    panels = [("val_acc", "validation accuracy [-]", False),
              ("artifact_bytes", "artifact bytes (log)", True),
              ("lat", "median latency (log, ms)", True)]
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(3, 3, figsize=(15, 12), sharex=True)
    for pidx, (pkey, ylabel, logy) in enumerate(panels):
        for idx, arch in enumerate(ARCHS):
            ax = axes[pidx][idx]
            xs, ys, labels = [], [], []
            for j, cond in enumerate(conds):
                r = fact.get((arch, cond))
                if r is None:
                    continue
                if pkey == "val_acc":
                    val = r.get("val_acc")
                elif pkey == "artifact_bytes":
                    val = r.get("artifact_bytes")
                else:
                    val = lat(r)
                if val is None:
                    continue
                xs.append(j); ys.append(float(val)); labels.append(cond_label[cond])
            if xs:
                ax.bar(xs, ys, 0.6, color=[plt.cm.tab10(i) for i in range(len(xs))])
                ax.set_xticks(xs)
                ax.set_xticklabels(labels, rotation=20, ha="right", fontsize=8)
                if logy:
                    ax.set_yscale("log")
                ax.set_ylabel(ylabel, fontsize=9)
                ax.grid(alpha=0.3, axis="y")
            if idx == 0:
                pass
            ax.set_title(arch.upper() if pidx == 0 else arch.upper(),
                         fontsize=10)
    _shared_legend(
        fig,
        [_h(plt.cm.tab10(i), cond_label[c], lw=1.4) for i, c in enumerate(conds)],
        title="condition", ncol=4, pad=0.12,
    )
    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0.12, 1, 1))
    _tight_savefig(fig, FIGURES / "factorial.png", dpi=150)
    cap = ("fig factorial.png: 3x3 grid (rows = metric: validation accuracy, artifact "
           "bytes, median latency; columns = MLP/CNN/GCN). One bar per condition: "
           "dense_fp32, sparse_fp32, dense_int8, sparse_int8 (the C2-selected INT8 "
           "method applied to dense and to the sparse operating point). Bytes and "
           "latency on log scale. Source: results/runs.jsonl, part=C, phase=factorial, "
           "status=ok, python 3.12 (C2 run).")
    cap_path = FIGURES / "CAPTIONS.md"
    with open(cap_path, "a") as f:
        f.write("\n## Part C (C2) factorial\n\n")
        f.write("- " + cap + "\n")
    print("wrote factorial.png + caption")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    import sys as _s
    if len([a for a in _s.argv[1:] if not a.startswith("-")]) == 0:
        main()
    if "size-latency" in _s.argv:
        precision_size_latency()
    if "factorial" in _s.argv:
        factorial_fig()

def _h(color, label, **kw) -> "plt.Line2D":
    h = plt.Line2D([], [], color=color, **kw)
    h.set_label(label)
    return h


def _shared_legend(fig, handles: list, title: str, ncol: int, pad: float) -> None:
    leg = fig.legend(
        handles, [h.get_label() for h in handles],
        title=title, loc="upper center", bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -pad),
        ncol=ncol, fontsize=8, title_fontsize=8, framealpha=0.9,
        handlelength=2.2, columnspacing=1.0,
    )
    # C1 review: verify the shared legend actually rendered (non-empty).
    assert leg.get_texts(), "shared legend rendered no text entries"
    return leg


def _tight_savefig(fig, path: Path, **kw) -> None:
    """Save with bbox_inches='tight' so the bottom shared legend is never
    clipped (C1 review), and disable minor tick labels on log axes to avoid
    overlapping labels (C1 review)."""
    for ax in fig.get_axes():
        for scale in ("x", "y"):
            axv = getattr(ax, f"get_{scale}scale", lambda: "linear")()
            if axv == "log":
                ax.minorticks_off()
    fig.savefig(path, bbox_inches="tight", **kw)

def _readable_ticks(ax) -> None:
    """C5: make every axis carry at least 2 visible tick labels.

    Log axes get 1/2/5 major ticks with plain-number formatting (minor ticks
    off); linear axes get a locator that guarantees >=2 majors. Used by the
    C2/C5 figures where narrow ranges made default log labels vanish.
    """
    import matplotlib.ticker as mtick
    for scale in ("x", "y"):
        axv = getattr(ax, f"get_{scale}scale", lambda: "linear")()
        loc = getattr(ax, f"get_{scale}majorlocator", None)
        if axv == "log":
            locator = mtick.LogLocator(subs=(1, 2, 5))
            setter = getattr(ax, f"set_{scale}majorlocator")
            setter(locator)
            getter = getattr(ax, f"get_{scale}majorlocator")
            if isinstance(getter(), mtick.LogLocator):
                fmt = mtick.ScalarFormatter()
                fmt.set_scientific(False)
                fmt.set_useOffset(False)
                getattr(ax, f"set_{scale}majorformatter")(fmt)
                ax.minorticks_off()
        else:
            getter = getattr(ax, f"get_{scale}majorlocator")
            lim = getattr(ax, f"get_{scale}lim")[1] - getattr(ax, f"get_{scale}lim")[0]
            if isinstance(loc, mtick.LinearLocator) and (loc.nbins <= 2 or not lim):
                setter = getattr(ax, f"set_{scale}majorlocator")
                setter(mtick.LinearLocator(nbins=max(2, int(lim / 1) + 2) if lim else 3))
            # default linear locator already gives >=2 labels; assert below.
        getter = getattr(ax, f"get_{scale}majorlocator")
        getter()
        labels = [t for t in getattr(ax, f"get_{scale}ticks")()
                  if ax.get_dataLim() is not None]
    # explicit assertion: >=2 visible major tick labels per axis
    for scale in ("x", "y"):
        getter = getattr(ax, f"get_{scale}majorlocator")
        ticks = getter().tick_values(getattr(ax, f"get_{scale}viewlim")[0],
                                     getattr(ax, f"get_{scale}viewlim")[1])
        assert len(ticks) >= 2, (
            f"C5: {scale} axis has {len(ticks)} tick labels (<2): {ticks}")

    for idx, arch in enumerate(ARCHS):
        ax = axes[idx]

        for j, fmt in enumerate(PRECISION_FORMATS):
            r = prec.get((arch, fmt))
            if r is None:

            lv = lat(r)

            xs.append(ab); ys.append(lv)
            labels.append(FORMAT_LABEL[fmt]); colors.append(fmt)
        # C5: dense seed-0 FP32 reference (latest factorial dense_fp32 row).
        fp32 = None

            for xi, yi, lb in zip(xs, ys, labels):
                ax.annotate(f"{lb}\n({xi:.4g} B, {yi:.3g} ms)",
                            (xi, yi), textcoords="offset points",

            allx = xs + ([ref_x] if ref_x else [])

            ax.grid(alpha=0.3, which="both")

def _readable_ticks(ax) -> None:
    """C5: make every axis carry at least 2 visible tick labels.

    Log axes get 1/2/5 major ticks with plain-number formatting (minor ticks
    off); linear axes keep their default locator (which yields >=2 labels).
    Used by the C2/C5 figures where narrow ranges made default log labels
    vanish.
    """
    import matplotlib.ticker as mtick
    for scale in ("x", "y"):
        is_log = getattr(ax, f"get_{scale}scale", lambda: "linear")() == "log"
        getter = getattr(ax, f"get_{scale}majorlocator")
        setter = getattr(ax, f"set_{scale}majorlocator")
        if is_log:
            setter(mtick.LogLocator(subs=(1, 2, 5)))
            fmt = mtick.ScalarFormatter()
            fmt.set_scientific(False)
            fmt.set_useOffset(False)
            if isinstance(getter(), mtick.FuncFormatter):
                # Keep custom formatters (e.g. KB) but ensure the locator has
                # enough ticks; plain-number formatter otherwise.
                loc = getter()
                if getattr(loc, "n", None) is not None and loc.n < 2:
                    setter(mtick.LogLocator(subs=(1, 2, 5)))
            else:
                getattr(ax, f"set_{scale}majorformatter")(fmt)
            ax.minorticks_off()
        # explicit assertion: >=2 visible major tick labels on this axis
        lo, hi = getattr(ax, f"get_{scale}viewlim")()
        ticks = getter().tick_values(lo, hi)
        assert len(ticks) >= 2, (
            f"C5: {scale} axis has {len(ticks)} tick labels (<2): {ticks}")

def _readable_ticks(ax) -> None:
    """C5: make every axis carry at least 2 visible tick labels.

    Log axes get 1/2/5 major ticks with plain-number formatting (minor ticks
    off); linear axes keep their default locator (which yields >=2 labels).
    Used by the C2/C5 figures where narrow ranges made default log labels
    vanish.
    """
    import matplotlib.ticker as mtick
    for scale in ("x", "y"):
        is_log = getattr(ax, f"get_{scale}scale", lambda: "linear")() == "log"
        getter = getattr(ax, f"get_{scale}majorlocator")
        setter = getattr(ax, f"set_{scale}majorlocator")
        if is_log:
            setter(mtick.LogLocator(subs=(1, 2, 5)))
            fmt = mtick.ScalarFormatter()
            fmt.set_scientific(False)
            fmt.set_useOffset(False)
            if isinstance(getter(), mtick.FuncFormatter):
                # Keep custom formatters (e.g. KB) but ensure the locator has
                # enough ticks; plain-number formatter otherwise.
                loc = getter()
                if getattr(loc, "n", None) is not None and loc.n < 2:
                    setter(mtick.LogLocator(subs=(1, 2, 5)))
            else:
                getattr(ax, f"set_{scale}majorformatter")(fmt)
            ax.minorticks_off()
        # explicit assertion: >=2 visible major tick labels on this axis
        lo, hi = getattr(ax, f"get_{scale}viewlim")()
        ticks = getter().tick_values(lo, hi)
        assert len(ticks) >= 2, (
            f"C5: {scale} axis has {len(ticks)} tick labels (<2): {ticks}")

def precision_size_latency() -> None:
    """C2 item 8a: figures/precision_size_latency.png. Per arch: artifact bytes
    vs batch-256 / full-graph median latency, one point per format (plus the
    dense seed-0 FP32 reference from the latest factorial dense_fp32 row),
    readable plain-number ticks, unsupported formats in the caption."""
    recs = _loads()
    FIGURES.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    prec = _c2_rows(recs, "precision")
    if not prec:
        print("no C2 phase=precision rows; skipping precision_size_latency")
        return

    def lat(r: dict) -> float | None:
        v = (r.get("latency") or {}).get(LAT_KEY[r["architecture"]]) or {}
        m = v.get("median_ms")
        return float(m) if isinstance(m, (int, float)) and m > 0 else None

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(15, 5))
    captions: list[str] = []
    for idx, arch in enumerate(ARCHS):
        ax = axes[idx]
        xs, ys, labels, colors = [], [], [], []
        for j, fmt in enumerate(PRECISION_FORMATS):
            r = prec.get((arch, fmt))
            if r is None:
                continue
            ab = r.get("artifact_bytes")
            lv = lat(r)
            if not ab or lv is None:
                continue
            xs.append(ab); ys.append(lv)
            labels.append(FORMAT_LABEL[fmt]); colors.append(fmt)
        # C5: dense seed-0 FP32 reference (latest factorial dense_fp32 row).
        fp32 = None
        for r in recs:
            if (r.get("part") == "C" and r.get("phase") == "factorial"
                    and r.get("status") == "ok" and r.get("architecture") == arch
                    and r.get("method") == "dense_fp32"
                    and (r.get("versions") or {}).get("python", "").startswith("3.12")):
                fp32 = r
        ref_x = ref_y = None
        if fp32 is not None:
            ref_x = fp32.get("artifact_bytes")
            ref_y = lat(fp32)
            if ref_x and ref_y is not None:
                xs.append(ref_x); ys.append(ref_y)
                labels.append("FP32 ref (dense)"); colors.append("fp32_ref")
        if xs:
            ax.scatter(xs, ys, s=60, color=[plt.cm.tab10(i % 10) for i in range(len(xs))],
                       marker=["o"] * (len(xs) - 1) + ["*"] if ref_x else "o",
                       s=[60] * (len(xs) - 1) + [110] if ref_x else 60,
                       zorder=3, edgecolors="k", linewidths=0.5)
            for xi, yi, lb in zip(xs, ys, labels):
                ax.annotate(f"{lb}\n({xi:.4g} B, {yi:.3g} ms)",
                            (xi, yi), textcoords="offset points",
                            xytext=(5, 3), fontsize=6.5)
            allx = xs + ([ref_x] if ref_x else [])
            ally = ys + ([ref_y] if ref_y else [])
            for scale, vals in (("x", allx), ("y", ally)):
                lo, hi = min(vals), max(vals)
                if hi / lo < 10:  # under 1 decade: linear axis is more readable
                    getattr(ax, f"set_{scale}scale")("linear")
                else:
                    getattr(ax, f"set_{scale}scale")("log")
                    pad = max((hi - lo), 1e-9) * 0.05
                    getattr(ax, f"set_{scale}lim")(lo / 1.06, hi * 1.06)
            ax.set_xlabel("artifact bytes")
            ax.set_ylabel(f"median latency (ms, {LAT_KEY[arch]})")
            ax.grid(alpha=0.3, which="both")
            _readable_ticks(ax)
        else:
            ax.axis("off")
        ax.set_title(arch.upper())
    # unsupported formats (not present for some arch) -> caption
    missing = []
    for arch in ARCHS:
        for fmt in PRECISION_FORMATS:
            if (arch, fmt) not in prec:
                missing.append(f"{arch}/{fmt}")
    _shared_legend(
        fig,
        [_h(plt.cm.tab10(i), FORMAT_LABEL[fmt]) for i, fmt in enumerate(PRECISION_FORMATS)],
        title="format", ncol=5, pad=0.10,
    )
    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0.12, 1, 1))
    _tight_savefig(fig, FIGURES / "precision_size_latency.png", dpi=150)
    cap = ("fig precision_size_latency.png: 3 panels (MLP, CNN, GCN). x: artifact bytes; "
           "y: median forward latency (ms; batch 256 for MLP/CNN, full graph for GCN). "
           "One point per format, each labeled with (bytes, ms); star = dense seed-0 "
           "FP32 reference (latest C2 factorial dense_fp32 row). Axes use plain-number "
           "1/2/5 log ticks when the range is >= 1 decade, linear otherwise. "
           "Source: results/runs.jsonl, part=C, phase=precision, status=ok, python 3.12 "
           "(C2 run); reference from phase=factorial. "
           + ("Unsupported/absent formats (not plotted): " + ", ".join(missing) + "."
              if missing else "All 5 formats present for all architectures."))
    captions.append(cap)
    plt.close(fig)

    cap_path = FIGURES / "CAPTIONS.md"
    with open(cap_path, "a") as f:
        f.write("\n## Part C (C2) size-latency\n\n")
        for c in captions:
            f.write("- " + c + "\n")
    print("wrote precision_size_latency.png + caption")

def factorial_fig() -> None:
    """C2 item 8b: figures/factorial.png. Per arch: accuracy, bytes, latency
    for the 4 conditions (dense_fp32, sparse_fp32, dense_int8, sparse_int8).
    Three sub-panels per arch (acc / bytes / latency), one point per condition."""
    recs = _loads()
    FIGURES.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    fact: dict[tuple[str, str], dict] = {}
    for r in recs:
        if (r.get("part") != "C" or r.get("phase") != "factorial"
                or r.get("status") != "ok"):
            continue
        py = (r.get("versions") or {}).get("python", "")
        if not py.startswith("3.12"):
            continue
        fact[(r["architecture"], r["method"])] = r
    if not fact:
        print("no C2 phase=factorial rows; skipping factorial.png")
        return

    conds = ("dense_fp32", "sparse_fp32", "dense_int8", "sparse_int8")
    cond_label = {"dense_fp32": "dense fp32", "sparse_fp32": "sparse fp32",
                  "dense_int8": "dense int8", "sparse_int8": "sparse int8"}

    def lat(r: dict) -> float | None:
        v = (r.get("latency") or {}).get(LAT_KEY[r["architecture"]]) or {}
        m = v.get("median_ms")
        return float(m) if isinstance(m, (int, float)) and m > 0 else None

    panels = [("val_acc", "validation accuracy [-]", False),
              ("artifact_bytes", "artifact bytes", True),
              ("lat", "median latency (ms)", True)]
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(3, 3, figsize=(15, 10), sharex=True)
    for pidx, (pkey, ylabel, logy) in enumerate(panels):
        for idx, arch in enumerate(ARCHS):
            ax = axes[pidx][idx]
            xs, ys, labels = [], [], []
            for j, cond in enumerate(conds):
                r = fact.get((arch, cond))
                if r is None:
                    continue
                if pkey == "val_acc":
                    val = r.get("val_acc")
                elif pkey == "artifact_bytes":
                    val = r.get("artifact_bytes")
                else:
                    val = lat(r)
                if val is None:
                    continue
                xs.append(j); ys.append(float(val)); labels.append(cond_label[cond])
            if xs:
                ax.bar(xs, ys, 0.6, color=[plt.cm.tab10(i) for i in range(len(xs))])
                ax.set_xticks(xs)
                ax.set_xticklabels(labels, rotation=20, ha="right", fontsize=8)
                if logy:
                    ax.set_yscale("log")
                # C5: value on top of every bar (bytes in KB, latency in ms with
                # 3 sig digits, accuracy with 4 decimals).
                top = max(ys)
                for xi, yi in zip(xs, ys):
                    if pkey == "val_acc":
                        txt = f"{yi:.4f}"
                    elif pkey == "artifact_bytes":
                        txt = f"{yi / 1024:.4g} KB"
                    else:
                        txt = f"{yi:.3g} ms"
                    ax.annotate(txt, (xi, yi), textcoords="offset points",
                                xytext=(0, 3), ha="center", fontsize=6.5)
                    if pkey != "val_acc":
                        top = max(top, yi * 1.6)
                if pkey == "val_acc":
                    ax.set_ylim(min(ys) - 0.02, max(ys) + 0.015)
                else:
                    ax.set_ylim(min(ys) / 1.1, max(ys) * 1.8)
                ax.set_ylabel(ylabel, fontsize=9)

# Figure captions

- fig acc_vs_sparsity.png: 3 panels (MLP, CNN, GCN). x: achieved sparsity of eligible weights (fraction zero, -); y: test accuracy (-). One line per method (color = method): dashed = post_prune, solid = post_finetune, seed-0 pilot (results/pilot_summary.csv, phase=pilot rows). Open P markers: confirmatory points, mean +/- sample std of test_acc over seeds 1-3 (results/confirm_summary.csv, stage=post_finetune). Horizontal reference lines (labeled in the shared legend, not on the plot): black = dense seed-0 test acc, gray = dense seed-0 val acc (results/baselines.md, Part A train seed-0); dotted black = dense_ft seed-0 (pilot). Source: results/pilot_summary.csv, results/confirm_summary.csv, results/baselines.md.

edits.oldText:
def _replace_caption_section(path: Path, header: str, caption: str) -> None:
    """C5: upsert a '## <header>' section (replace all existing copies) so
    re-running the figure script does not duplicate captions."""
    lines = path.read_text().splitlines(keepends=True) if path.exists() else []
    kept = [l for l in lines if not l.startswith(header)]
    # drop a single separator left behind by removing the last section line
    out = "".join(kept)
    # insert the (single) section right before the first existing '## ' header,
    # or at the end if there is none.
    inserted = f"\n{header}\n\n- {caption}\n\n"
    text = out if out.endswith("\n") else out + "\n"
    idx = 0
    for pos, l in enumerate(text.splitlines(keepends=True)):
        if l.startswith("## "):
            idx = pos
            break
    else:
        idx = len(text.splitlines(keepends=True))
    ls = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
    ls.insert(idx, inserted)
    path.write_text("".join(ls))
